items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: He had a lengthy association with trumpeter Ted Curson

ctx.x: One of the great voices of the baritone saxophone, Nick Brignola was born in Troy, NY on July 17, 1936. He attended Ithaca and Berklee Colleges but was largely self taught and by the late ‘50s Nick had recorded with Herb Pomeroy and Cal Tjader. He had a lengthy association with trumpeter Ted Curson interspersed with short stints in the bands of Woody Herman and Sal Salvador.

Nick experimented with fusion as a leader of his own group, but is known today as the leading exponent of hard bop baritone sax. He has recorded numerous albums on a number of labels including “Baritone Madness” where he is joined by fellow baritonist Pepper Adams. Nick can be heard at jazz festivals and parties and often offers up an unusual original sound on a rarely seen metal clarinet.
